text: Git branching is an important part of a version control workflow. A branch lets you work on new code without affecting the main project. Developers often create feature branches to build new features or fix bugs safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main code. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This process helps catch mistakes early and keeps the project organized. By using branches, pull requests, and merging, teams can work together more easily and keep their code stable.
